# Growth Team Partner Incident Checklist

## When this checklist applies

Use this checklist for any incident that affects a current partner experience, partner deliverable, partner workflow, or a partner-facing launch owned by Growth.

## Owner

- The Growth engineer covering partner comms owns the first outbound note and all follow-ups until a clear handoff is named in the incident thread.
- The covering Growth engineer may send the first outbound note without extra approval.

## First outbound note deadline

- Send the very first note to the affected partner by the following business day at the latest.
- If the incident is confirmed during business hours and the facts are already clear enough to describe impact, send the note the same day instead of waiting.

## Before sending

- Confirm the partner name, impacted feature or workflow, and the best active contact channel.
- State only confirmed facts.
- If root cause or timing is still unknown, say that directly.
- Include the next update time in the message, even if the update is only to say work is still in progress.

## First outbound note must include

- A plain statement that we are aware of the issue.
- What the partner may be seeing or unable to do.
- When the issue started, if known.
- What the partner should do right now, if anything.
- The time of the next update.
- The name or role of the Growth owner following the incident.

## Send-now template

Subject: Update on [issue] affecting [partner name]

Hi [partner name],

We’re aware of an issue affecting [feature/workflow] for [partner/account name]. Right now, the impact is [short impact statement]. The issue started at [time] / We are still confirming when it began.

Our team is actively working on it. For now, please [recommended action, or "hold off on retrying until our next update"].

I’ll send the next update by [day, time, timezone], even if we are still investigating.

[Name or "Growth Engineering"]

## Follow-up cadence

- Send an update at the time promised in the last note.
- Keep sending updates at least once per business day until the incident is resolved or the partner confirms they no longer need active updates.
- Send a resolution note once impact is cleared.

## Resolution note must include

- What is fixed.
- Whether any partner action is required.
- Whether any data, deliverable, or workflow needs to be rerun or checked.
- Who to contact if the partner still sees issues.

A design doc is mandatory for any change that touches two or more services. In plain terms: if the work crosses the boundary from one service into a second service, write the design doc before implementation starts.

Example: if a change updates the API service and also requires coordinated changes in the queue worker, that is a two-service change and needs a design doc.

Company standups are a live, synchronous meeting for everyone; there is no async written substitute. Start with brief ritual cites first, then move into open floor updates, questions, and blockers. Keep ritual notes compact, keep the full standup to 30 minutes or less, and move any extended chatter or follow-ups into the relevant channel after the meeting.

## Bug Triage Cadence

Bug triage runs once each day and rotates across the platform engineering team.

Each bug triage session should list one named owner for that day. If no owner is published for a Monday session, bug triage does not run on Monday.

- Before attendees leave: give each action item a short title, one clear next step, a status (`open`), and a link to the source note, thread, or ticket if one exists.

- Within 1 business day: post the action-item list in the team workspace so anyone can see what was created and what is still unassigned.

2. Add the payment reason, owner, due date, and any ticket or vendor context needed for handoff.
3. Check the total:

4. If any invoice detail is unclear, stop the handoff and resolve it in the thread first.
5. Follow this handoff order before funds are sent:

   - Finance reviews first for invoices at `$10,000` or above.
   - After finance review, or immediately for invoices under `$10,000`, hand off for payment processing.
   - Funds go out only after the required review path is complete.
6. Post the final status in the thread so the next owner is clear.

# Growth Team Partner Incident Checklist

Use this checklist when a partner-facing incident affects a Growth-owned partner experience and someone on Growth is covering communications.

## 1. Confirm this needs a partner note

- Send a partner note if the incident is partner-facing and could change what the affected partner sees, receives, or is waiting on.
- If impact is still being confirmed but a specific partner is likely affected, treat it as partner-facing and prepare the first note now.

## 2. Send the very first outbound note on time

- Deadline: send the first outbound note to the affected partner by the following business day.
- Do not wait for extra approval from Growth leadership or another reviewer before sending that first note.
- If you are the comms cover, you are authorized to send the first note as soon as you have the minimum facts below.

Minimum facts required before sending:

- What happened in plain language.
- What the partner may be experiencing.
- Whether there is a current workaround, if any.
- When we will update them next.

## 3. Use this first-note structure

Subject: Issue affecting [partner-facing workflow]

Hi [Partner Name],

We’re reaching out because we identified an issue affecting [brief workflow or feature]. Right now, this may cause [plain-language impact].

Our team is actively working on it. [Include workaround if one exists: "For now, you can ..."].

We’ll send the next update by [time and timezone] even if the issue is not fully resolved yet.

Thanks,
[Your name]
Growth Engineering

## 4. Log the note and keep updates moving

- Post in the team thread or incident thread when the first partner note has been sent.
- Include the send time, partner name, and the promised next-update time.
- If the issue remains open, send the next update at the promised time even if the update is only that work is still in progress.

## 5. Close the loop

- Send a resolution note once the partner-facing impact is resolved or no longer applies.
- Include what changed, whether any follow-up action is needed from the partner, and who to contact if they still see the issue.

- If there is a tradeoff or limitation, state it in 1 short clause instead of burying it in soft language.
- Avoid team-internal process talk; cut mentions of reviews, tickets, handoffs, or who helped unless the blurb explicitly needs attribution.

# Retro Follow-Up Checklist

Use this right after every `team:growth` retrospective.

- [ ] Create one action-item entry per decision before the retro ends.
- [ ] Fill every required field within 30 minutes of wrap.
- [ ] Post the completed action-item list in the team workspace the same day.
- [ ] Re-ping any action item still missing fields after 30 minutes.

## Required fields for each action item

- `Action`: one clear verb-led step.
- `Owner`: one directly responsible person.
- `Why now`: the issue or risk this action is meant to reduce.
- `Due`: a concrete date, not "soon" or "next week."
- `Status`: start as `open`.
- `Check-in point`: the next team moment where we expect an update, usually the next standup or planning touchpoint.

## Completion standard

- [ ] Every action item has all six required fields filled within 30 minutes of retro wrap.
- [ ] Every owner has acknowledged their item before end of day.
- [ ] Any action tied to staging, warehouse, billing, or review flow includes the exact artifact to inspect on follow-up.
- [ ] Any action without an owner or due date is not carried forward; assign it or drop it before the day ends.

## Paste-ready action-item template

```md
- Action:
  Owner:
  Why now:
  Due:
  Status: open
  Check-in point:
```

# Growth Runbook Maintenance Checklist

## Purpose

Keep every active Growth runbook current, easy to use under pressure, and ready for formal review after a major incident.

## Refresh Cadence

- Do a recurring runbook refresh once per quarter.
- Review any runbook used during a major incident within two business days after the incident closes.
- Review any runbook affected by a shipped flow change, tooling change, alert change, or ownership change within five business days of that change.

## Who Tracks The Next Due Date

- Each runbook has one named Growth owner.
- The runbook owner updates and tracks the next due date in the runbook header.
- Kofi carries the team-level checklist in the Growth meeting agenda and calls out any runbook due in the next fourteen days.

## What Kicks Off The Update Process

- The next quarterly due date arrives.
- A major incident happens and the runbook was used, skipped, or found incomplete.
- A production workflow, experiment flow, alert, dashboard, or escalation path changes.
- The runbook owner or backup changes.

## Runbook Header Standard

Every Growth runbook should show:

- Runbook name
- Owner
- Backup reviewer
- Last reviewed date
- Next due date
- Linked dashboards, alerts, and source docs
- Slack channel or escalation contact to use during active work

## Meeting Checklist

- Confirm the list of active Growth runbooks is complete.
- Check whether any runbook is due now or due within the next fourteen days.
- Confirm each runbook still has a named owner and backup reviewer.
- Confirm linked dashboards, alerts, and docs still open the right destinations.
- Confirm the steps still match the current product flow and tooling.
- Remove stale references, retired experiments, and dead follow-up steps.
- Add any missing decision points, handoff notes, or rollback steps found in recent use.
- Mark the runbook as reviewed and set the next due date before the meeting ends.

## Update Flow

1. The runbook owner opens the update when a trigger happens.
2. The owner makes the content changes and tags a backup reviewer for a skim.
3. The reviewer checks that the steps are accurate, concrete, and usable during live work.
4. The owner updates the last reviewed date and next due date in the header.
5. Kofi notes completion in the next Growth team meeting.

## Formal Review Rule

- Growth runbooks get formal review after major incidents happen.
- If no major incident triggered formal review, the quarterly refresh still happens on schedule.

## Handbook Update: Standup Expectations

Company standups are synchronous sessions and do not have an async written substitute. Keep the meeting to 30 minutes or less. Run the session in this order: brief ritual notes and citations first, then open questions and discussion. Keep ritual updates compact so the group can move quickly into anything that needs live attention.

For next cycle, keep sprint spillover to no more than two unfinished tickets per squad.
Spillover counts any ticket committed for the sprint that is not done by close, including work still waiting on review, validation, or release.
If your squad is above two, cut next-cycle scope and post the owners plus a recovery plan before kickoff.

## Platform Weekly Sync Notes Checklist

- Add the meeting title and date at the top before the call starts.
- List attendees as they join and note any expected absences.
- Capture each decision as it happens in one line.
- Add an owner to every decision that needs follow-up.
- Add a concrete due date to every action item before the topic closes.
- Record blockers live, including who is blocked and what is needed to unblock them.
- Link any ticket, doc, or runbook mentioned if it is needed for follow-up this week.
- Mark any item that needs async follow-up in the channel after the meeting.
- Keep notes concise enough to finish within the live discussion; do not leave placeholders for decisions, owners, or due dates.
- Before the meeting ends, do a 60-second readback of decisions, owners, and due dates to confirm the record is complete.

# Bug Triage Coverage for Next Quarter

For next quarter, company bug triage will run with one published Platform contact at a time. The named contact is the first stop for new bug intake, initial severity checks, owner assignment, and cross-team follow-up for issues raised by Support, Product, or Engineering.

We will change the named contact on a monthly cadence. The active contact will be posted at the start of each month and referenced in the shared bug-triage channel and intake note. During that month, route all new bugs through that person unless an updated coverage notice is posted.

## How To Route Issues

- Support: send customer-reported bugs to the active triage contact with impact, customer scope, reproduction details, and any ticket link.
- Product: send newly confirmed product defects to the active triage contact with expected behavior, actual behavior, launch or roadmap risk, and screenshots or logs if available.
- Engineering: send regressions, incidents, and internally found defects to the active triage contact with service, environment, severity, and the best available reproduction steps.

If the listed contact drops out mid-cycle because of leave, incident load, or schedule change, do not wait for the next monthly turnover. Post the issue in the shared bug-triage channel and tag `Platform Triage`; the Platform manager on duty will publish the replacement contact the same business day. Until that update lands, urgent issues should continue through the shared channel so intake and severity decisions do not pause.

## July Through August Example

Example:

- July 1 through July 31: Diego is the named bug-triage contact.
- August 1 through August 31: Mei becomes the named bug-triage contact.

If Diego is the listed contact for July and becomes unavailable on July 18, route any new issue to the shared bug-triage channel and tag `Platform Triage` immediately. Platform will name the replacement for the rest of the July cycle, and that replacement will stay active until the scheduled August 1 handoff to Mei unless a new coverage update is posted sooner.

This model is meant to keep intake simple: check the currently published contact first, and if that person drops out mid-cycle, move the issue into the shared bug-triage path so Platform can reassign coverage without blocking the report.

Squad leads should keep sprint spillover to no more than three unfinished tickets per squad for the next cycle.

Spillover counts any ticket committed in the current sprint that is not done by sprint close and moves into the next cycle, whether it is unstarted, in progress, or waiting on review.

If your squad is above the cap, cut scope before planning closes and flag the exception with the reason and recovery plan in the planning channel.
